recommendedNewSections.heading: Project Management Software for Specific Small Business Industries
recommendedNewSections.reason: Competitors generally list software but don't deeply explore how different industries (e.g., marketing, construction, IT, consulting) might have unique needs that specific PM tools address better. This adds practical, targeted value.
recommendedNewSections.suggestedOutline: H3: For Marketing Agencies; H3: For IT & Software Development; H3: For Consulting Firms; H3: For Creative Teams

recommendedNewSections.heading: Beyond Features: Evaluating Customer Support and Training for Small Businesses
recommendedNewSections.reason: Small businesses often lack dedicated IT or project management staff, making robust customer support, onboarding, and training resources critical for successful adoption and long-term use. This is a common pain point not explicitly covered.
recommendedNewSections.suggestedOutline: H3: Types of Support Available (Chat, Email, Phone); H3: Onboarding & Training Resources; H3: Community & Knowledge Base

recommendedNewSections.heading: Maximizing ROI: Measuring the Impact of PM Software on Your Small Business
recommendedNewSections.reason: While some competitors mention 'calculate total value,' a dedicated section on how small businesses can actually measure the return on investment (time saved, increased efficiency, better project outcomes) would be highly valuable and differentiate the content.
recommendedNewSections.suggestedOutline: H3: Key Metrics to Track; H3: Case Studies & Success Stories; H3: Long-Term Benefits

recommendedNewSections.heading: Common Pitfalls to Avoid When Choosing Project Management Software
recommendedNewSections.reason: Competitor 1 touches on 'avoid costly errors' but a dedicated section outlining common mistakes (e.g., over-featuring, ignoring user adoption, not planning for scalability) would help readers make informed decisions and prevent costly mistakes.
recommendedNewSections.suggestedOutline: H3: Over-Complicating Your Needs; H3: Neglecting User Adoption; H3: Underestimating Integration Requirements; H3: Ignoring Scalability
